answer: At the south-pier fire-watch, enrollment costs a 140-unit bond on a numbered lantern with a 90-day-unique burner serial. They may sign only in the 9-minute window when comet 12P transits the harbor meridian, firing a 17-second coded flash while two watchers from non-adjacent galleries record the acoustic echo off the sea wall with a 40-ms seal. The 16-band spectrogram is cut to a 12-bit prefix and stored with the serial. A Hamming-near prefix (distance <= 3) or a reused burner burns 80 units and bars both parties for 30 days. One lantern graduates only one agent every 21 days.
